title: Add urgent priority and a command to set priority by record
summary: Add an Urgent level above High in plan ordering. Add a CLI command that appends a priority record for a queued request, and plan/status use it over the request text's priority. The reader prompt tells the reader to mark speed requests urgent with a reason in the reading. Audience: Athena's operator and the reader agent.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added for each acceptance item; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check ordering, override and reading behavior by running tests.
One focused change on the listed files.
Docs, changelog and decision entry written for outside readers.
Ranking is changed in plan ordering, not by re-queuing.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The priority record is a new record kind in athena-data records.rs; the latest record per request wins.
Urgent set by the reader is carried in the reading (with a reason field) and can be overridden by the command record.
Plan order: dependencies first, then priority (record over text), then rung, then age, as today.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a plan test shows urgent ordered before high, high before normal, with a dependency still ordered first even when the dependent is urgent.

Run cargo test: a test shows a priority record for a queued request overrides the priority in its text, and the order shown by plan and the priority shown by status change accordingly, with no new request record written.
Run cargo test: a reading test shows a speed-improving request gets urgent with a recorded reason in the reading, and an ordinary request does not.

The new CLI command appends a priority record (append-only; the request is not rewritten), rejects unknown priority values and unknown or non-queued requests with a clear error, and Priority::from_text parses 'Priority: urgent'.

reader.md defines when to mark urgent (makes Athena faster or cuts wasted time: failed/rejected attempts, planning stops, timeouts, redo-work retries, thrash, duplicated checks) and requires the reason in the reading; main.rs help text mentions urgent and the command.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry and docs/decisions.md records the decision with alternatives considered.
cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean and the full cargo test passes.

out_of_scope: Changing queue storage or making requests mutable
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Automatic urgent marking beyond the reader's judgment
departures: Multi-crate change with a new record kind, CLI command and reader schema change, so cost and time are above the reference.
